reviews.review:
Borderlands Schmorderlands. 

If you want a well designed endlessly replayable co-op loot shooter that doesn't lobotomise you with ♥♥♥♥♥♥ humour and runs well on a potato (not to mention a 5090) this is the game for you.
It is great making the most broken build possible only to realize that you indeed can still get one shot. 10/10 would sacrifice 75% of my life for a buff again.

The game at its core is fun and has lots of variety, but at times it feels like it hates its own players.

Core gameplay loop (outside of the obvious - it being a rogue-lite) is Borderlands-like where you need to have the right element to deal the good damage to an enemy (shielded enemies take more damage from lighting weapons, armoured enemies take more damage from corrosive damage) which feels like a bit of a problem in a game with fully randomised weapons with every run that you do. You can't control what weapon you start with, you just have to hope you get the right damage type, and if you don't then have to hope that you can craft a build with absurdly high base DPS to make the shields/armour negligible. That doesn't feel super fun, in all honestly. The shooty gameplay with skills you can use is fun, though!

Secondly, you move like a snail with a pathetically short dash move. Compared to other shooters of similar gameplay loop, I don't quite understand why characters feel like they have weights strapped to their legs with how slow they move and the dash move being really short distance and not providing invincibility frames by default (I assume there's an upgrade you can find mid-run for that). My muscle memory from playing other games that rely on dodging to survive (mainly Guild Wars 2, admittedly) just gets confused when I dash and still get killed.

Finally, prepare to die and feel like it was absolutely unfair. Majority of my deaths in other roguelites like Risk of Rain (1/2), Hades (1/2) and RoboQuest feel like they were my own fault - I dodged into a clearly visible enemy attack, I got too close to the enemies, I damaged myself on an environment trap/explosive, etc. This game has yet to give me that feeling, instead it feels like "there was no way I could have dodged it" or "there was no way I could have seen where and how I got damaged". There is, IMHO, a serious problem of readability of boss attacks. Quite frankly I don't know how this game has been out for as long as it was and it still feels unfinished.

ok I complained a lot but credit where credit is due - the gameplay did hook me in eventually once I got more upgrades and it's ABSOLUTELY better in co-op than in single-player. The bots you can play with are cardboard cutouts that exist to soak up enemy damage and revive you.
Game fun as heck. 1000% worth the purchase.

Honestly? I like it. Simple, fun, chaotic roguelite shooter. Hop in, blast enemies, grab some OP scrolls, and suddenly you’re way stronger than you should be.

The characters are cute and cool, and the weapon variety keeps it fresh. Mixing weapons with scrolls makes every run feel different, with a lot of replay value if you’re into that kind of thing.

Solo is fine, but co-op is where it really shines. Performance is smooth, way better than most big titles lately. My only gripe is it can feel grindy solo — but that’s the roguelite deal.

If you like Borderlands-style chaos in a run-based setup, this one’s worth it.
